judge_assessment.explanation: Every arithmetic claim the judge makes is exact and I re-derived all of it independently: floor/ceiling for 47 (6,7) and 150 (12,13); sqrt(30)=5.4772 -> 5.5; sqrt(83)=9.1104 -> 9.1; sqrt(41)=6.4031 -> 6.4; sqrt(45)=6.7082 -> 6.7; sqrt(132)=11.4891 -> 11.5; sqrt(50)=7.0711 -> 7.1; sqrt(20)=4.4721 < 4.5; and 2.7 < sqrt(8)=2.8284 < 3.1 < sqrt(10)=3.1623. The judge's claim about the marked point is also exact: P is drawn at tikz x=6 on a line ticked 7.0..8.0 in tenths, i.e. 7.6, and 7.6^2=57.76 with 7.7^2=59.29, so only 58 of {55,58,62} lands there. Two things the judge did not look at, both visible in the delivered PDFs, keep this from being a clean 32/32 on answer_key_quality. (1) The Quick Answers bank on answer_key.pdf page 1 prints '4. -' for problem 4, whose relation IS machine-verified: gate_log.txt line 27 reads '[PASS] Problem 4: compare(sqrt(20) vs 4.5) -> < (expected <)'. render_quick_answers._fmt calls bare sympy.sympify on the string '<', which raises, and the except branch returns the em-dash reserved for manual-only items. A grader reading the bank gets no answer at all for one of the ten problems. (2) Problem 10 prints three response slots - plot sqrt(50), give it to the nearest tenth, and 'explain in one sentence why Nadia's rounding rule gives the wrong tenth'. verify.json id 10 is a single approx entry (7.1) and there is no manual entry anywhere in the file; machine_observation confirms gate_chain_manual_flags=false. final_response.md does not merely omit this, it argues for it in writing: 'The written explanation in problem 10 is a bonus on top of a numeric answer that is checked, so the problem is not left unverified.' That is precisely the reasoning the manual-flag rule exists to forbid, and SKILL.md line 257 already says the opposite ('Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer').

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 inverts the task instead of repeating it: the point P is pre-marked and the student must decide which of sqrt(55), sqrt(58), sqrt(62) belongs there. The key's method is the reason this works - square the tick rather than estimate three roots (7.6^2 = 57.76, 7.7^2 = 59.29, so only 58 lies between) - and both wrong choices are declared as trap objects in verify.json with the values 7.4 and 7.9 that a student would actually produce.

Every one of the ten problems carries its own number line drawn at the scale that problem needs - integers 0..10 for problem 1, 10..15 for problem 2, and tenths windows 5.0-6.0, 4.0-5.0, 9.0-10.0, 7.0-8.0, 2.6-3.6, 6.0-7.0, 11.0-12.0 for the estimation items - so the plotted dot is the work rather than a decoration, which is exactly what 'representations-applications' asks for.

Problem 7's four values are chosen so eyeballing fails: 3.1 versus sqrt(10) = 3.1623 differ by six hundredths, and the key names the trap explicitly ('3.1 and sqrt(10) look close, but 3.1^2 = 9.61 < 10').

The study guide states one rule at the top - for positive numbers squaring preserves order - and then every skill box uses that single rule, including the try-its (sqrt(90) between 9 and 10, sqrt(68) approx 8.2, sqrt(23) approx 4.8 'a hair left of 4.8'), all of which I checked and all of which are right.

root_causes.description: An explanation slot attached to a problem that also has a numeric answer is treated as covered by the numeric check. Nothing in the gate chain looks at the worksheet's imperative verbs, so a problem that says 'explain in one sentence why' can pass with a single approx entry and the run reports zero manual items. SKILL.md already states the correct rule in prose; there is no mechanism that enforces it.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 10: 'Plot sqrt(50) on the number line, give its value to the nearest tenth, and explain in one sentence why Nadia's rounding rule gives the wrong tenth.'
verify.json id 10 is one approx entry (sqrt(50) -> 7.1); the file contains no entry of type manual.
machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags = false and gate_log.txt ends 'BUILD PASSED - all gates green' with no manual-review line.

final_response.md states the rationalisation directly: 'All 13 passed; nothing is flagged for manual review. The written explanation in problem 10 is a bonus on top of a numeric answer that is checked, so the problem is not left unverified.'

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt resolves a string expected by calling bare sympy.sympify. A relation operator is not a sympifiable expression, so the call raises and the handler returns '---', the same glyph the module documents as meaning 'manual-only: see solution'. A verified answer is therefore printed as an absence.
evidence: scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61: the str branch is try: sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)) / except (SympifyError, SyntaxError, TypeError, ValueError): return '---'.
verify.json id 4: {type: compare, values: ['sqrt(20)', '4.5'], order: relation, expected: '<'}.
answer_key.pdf page 1 Quick Answers prints '4. -' while answer_key.tex problem 4 boxes 'sqrt(20) < 4.5'.

improvements.title: Gate the worksheet source for explanation verbs and require a manual entry on that problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate step that scans each worksheet problem block for open-response imperatives ('explain', 'why', 'justify', 'describe', 'name the', 'say which', 'in your own words', 'sketch', 'draw', 'mark') and fails the build unless that problem id carries at least one verify.json entry of type manual. The check belongs next to tests/check_answer_key.py so it runs inside the existing gate chain, and SKILL.md should state the rule in the enforceable form the current prose only implies: a numeric check on the same problem never covers an explanation slot; a problem may be both machine-verified and manual, and the mixed case is the normal one for error-analysis items.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture built from this case: worksheet problem 10's text ('Plot sqrt(50) ... and explain in one sentence why Nadia's rounding rule gives the wrong tenth') plus a verify.json whose id 10 holds only {type: approx, expr: 'sqrt(50)', expected: 7.1}. The new check must exit non-zero naming problem 10's explanation slot. Adding {id: 10, type: manual, desc: 'why rounding the radicand to the nearest perfect square gives the wrong tenth'} must make the same fixture pass and must move the run's exit code from 0 to 2 (green with manual items).
improvements.expected_impact: Turns the single largest systemic gap in this run into a build failure instead of an author judgement call. On curr-203 it converts a silently unreviewed sentence into a declared manual item and stops final_response.md claiming 'nothing is flagged for manual review' on a sheet that ends with an explain-why problem.
improvements.risk: Verb matching will fire on directions text and on phrases like 'show the two tenths you squared' that are work-shown rather than answer slots, so the matcher must be scoped to the problem body and given a short allowlist; expect a modest increase in manual items per sheet, which is the intended cost.

improvements.title: Render verified compare relations in the Quick Answers bank instead of the manual em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers._fmt, special-case a relation string before sympify: for expected values in {'<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!='} emit the operator with the compared values around it, taking them from the entry's 'values' list (so problem 4 renders as 'sqrt(20) < 4.5' rather than a bare glyph). Pass the whole entry, not just entry['expected'], into the formatter so 'values' is reachable, and reserve '---' strictly for ids whose only entries are type manual.
improvements.regression_test: Feed render_quick_answers.py this task's verify.json and assert the rendered row for id 4 contains a relation and not '---'. The assertion fails on today's renderer (the bank in the shipped answer_key.pdf prints '4. -') and passes after the fix. Pair it with an id whose only entry is type manual to assert '---' still appears there, so the two cases stay distinguishable.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores a printed answer for every verified comparison on the grading page. In this batch alone the same bug blanks 1 row here, 2 in curr-204, 4 in curr-205, 1 in curr-207, 2 in curr-220 and 8 of 10 in curr-231.
improvements.risk: Rows carrying a long relation widen the bank and can drop it from four columns to two; column_count already adapts, but the relation form should be abbreviated (operator only) when the compared expressions are long.

case_summary: A number-line workshop whose mathematics is fully correct - I re-derived all thirteen checks and every plot position, rounding and ordering claim in the answer key, and found no error - and whose design genuinely serves the focus: each of the ten problems carries a number line at its own scale, problem 6 inverts the task by marking P first, and problem 7 is engineered so eyeballing fails. Two defects survive the ACCEPT. The Quick Answers bank prints '4. -' for a compare that gate_log.txt records as PASS, because _fmt sympifies the string '<' and falls back to the manual glyph; a grader gets no answer for that problem. And problem 10's 'explain in one sentence why' is recorded as a plain approx entry, with final_response.md arguing explicitly that the numeric answer makes the explanation verified - the exact reasoning SKILL.md's manual rule forbids. Neither defect touches the mathematics, so the ACCEPT stands, but both are in the delivered teacher-facing artifact.
